holidays.name: National Cook for Your Pets Day
holidays.description: A day for pet owners to put down the kibble bag and whip up a homemade meal for their furry, feathered, or scaly companions. Think chicken-and-rice bowls for Fido and tuna treats for Whiskers.
holidays.origin: Created by pet lifestyle author and animal enthusiast Colleen Paige, who founded many of the unofficial national pet holidays, to encourage owners to prepare healthy homemade meals for their animals.
holidays.funFact: Before commercial pet food took off in the early 1900s, most pets ate table scraps and home-cooked meals, so your dog's great-great-grandpup was basically a home-cooking connoisseur.

holidays.name: National Vinegar Day
holidays.description: A tangy tribute to the sour liquid that cleans your windows, pickles your cucumbers, and dresses your salad. Celebrate by cooking with it, cleaning with it, or just sniffing it dramatically.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance celebrating vinegar, one of humanity's oldest condiments, with a history that stretches back roughly 10,000 years to ancient Babylon, where it was made from dates.
holidays.funFact: The word vinegar comes from the French 'vin aigre,' meaning 'sour wine,' because it was originally what happened when wine was accidentally left out too long.

holidays.name: World Vegan Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of plant-based living, when people try out dairy-free and meat-free meals, share recipes, and show off that jackfruit really can pretend to be pulled pork.
holidays.origin: Established in 1994 by Louise Wallis, then president of The Vegan Society UK, to mark the organization's 50th anniversary. November 1 was chosen as it fell around Halloween and the end of the Celtic harvest festival season.
holidays.funFact: The term 'vegan' was coined in 1944 by Donald Watson, who took the first three and last two letters of 'vegetarian' because veganism was 'the beginning and end of vegetarianism.'

holidays.name: Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) Begins
holidays.description: A vibrant Mexican holiday where families welcome back the spirits of deceased loved ones with colorful altars, marigolds, sugar skulls, and their favorite foods. It is a joyful party for the departed rather than a sad occasion.
holidays.origin: Rooted in Aztec rituals honoring the dead, blended with Catholic All Saints' Day traditions after the Spanish arrived. November 1 traditionally honors deceased children, and November 2 honors adults.
holidays.funFact: The bright orange cempasúchil marigolds used on the altars are believed to guide spirits home with their vivid color and strong scent.

holidays.name: National Author's Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the people who stare at blank pages for a living. Celebrate by reading a favorite book, thanking a writer, or finally admitting you will never finish your own novel.
holidays.origin: Established in 1928 when Nellie Verne Walker Burt of Bement, Illinois, proposed the day to the General Federation of Women's Clubs, and the U.S. Department of Commerce recognized it in 1949.
holidays.funFact: November 1 also kicks off National Novel Writing Month (NaNoWriMo) tradition for many hopeful writers, who attempt to write 50,000 words in 30 days.
